by: google/gemini-3.8-flash (machine translation of the OCR text, 20-Nov-2026; not checked)
segments: ... {OCR?} the sons of the king and his nobles hastened and went to meet the Egyptians,
and they encountered them beside the Rock of Sarvand.
And the Armenians were defeated,
and the lord of wages {OCR? i.e. Leon, the King's eldest son} was captured on Tuesday the 24th
of the month of Ab of this year.
And Baron Thoros, the younger son of the king, was killed,
and the rest of his nobles fled.
And the Egyptians entered and spread over the whole land of Cilicia,
and they caused great devastation, slaughter, and captivity in it.
And Sis they burned with fire,
and the great church they destroyed,
and indeed all the churches.
And none escaped except two churches of ours:
that of the Mother of God,
and that of Mar Bar Sauma,
because there was no wood in their construction.
And they plundered Mopsuestia, and Ayas, and Adana,
and took into captivity countless sons and daughters.
To Tarsus, however, they did not reach.
The monastery of Paximad they burned,
but that of Gwikat they did not harm,
because a monk was found in it who spoke Arabic,
and he prostrated himself before them,
and they did not harm him,
nor his monastery.
And they remained in the land, plundering and burning, for twenty days,
and they departed.
King Hethum,
after they had departed,
arrived,
and with him an army of the Tatars and of the Romans {i.e. of Rum/Seljuks}.
And these, instead of help, caused damage;
and what was left from the Egyptians,
they plundered.
And after these things,
King Hethum began to care for the redemption of his son.
And while he was promising gold and fortresses to the Egyptian {sultan} that he would give as the price of his son,
he replied:
"Except for a friend that I have among the Tatars,
whose name is Sunqur al-Ashqar,
that is, the reddish-blonde,
I ask nothing of you.
Rescue this man and send him to me,
and take your son."
And in this same year,
Rukn al-Din, the ruler of Rum, wanted to destroy the Parwana,
the one who had established him on the royal throne,
and by whose good management his affairs were prospering.
Therefore, when the Parwana found this out,
he informed the Mongol nobles while Rukn al-Din was with them.
He urged {OCR?} a certain man,
and he entered upon him in the tent in which he was dining,
and threw a bowstring around his neck
